Right: walking forward from C through B and D, the first match is F (value 7), which becomes the selection. G also matches but is never reached, because the walk stops at F; A matches but lies against the arrows." width="100%"} From each currently selected node, walks forward along outgoing edges in breadth-first order and stops each branch at the first node that satisfies `conditions=`. Matching nodes are not expanded further, so anything beyond them is never visited. Branches that never match keep going until they run out of outgoing edges or until `max_steps=` hops have been taken. When the walk finishes, the node selection is replaced by the result. This is useful for: - finding the nearest downstream node of a given kind (e.g., the first "approval" step after a task, or the first warehouse reachable from a supplier) - locating the boundary where an attribute crosses a threshold along directed paths - collecting everything traversed on the way to such a boundary (with `add_to_selection=True, exclude_unmatched=False`) Things to keep in mind: - each starting node is traversed independently; the results are combined - a starting node that already satisfies the condition is kept as-is and not expanded - in undirected graphs every neighbor counts as an outward neighbor, so the walk spreads in all directions - if no nodes are selected, the method does nothing - `conditions=` is a Python callable invoked once per visited node (and again on some nodes when building the final selection), so very large traversals are bounded by Python speed ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [conditions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [callable]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A callable that receives a node ID (an `int`) and returns `True` when the walk should stop at that node. Node attributes can be read inside the callable, e.g., with `graph.get_node(node_id).attributes`. The callable is evaluated on the starting nodes too. [max_steps]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[30]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of hops taken outward from each starting node. Default is `30`. When a branch reaches this depth without a match, the last frontier of unmatched nodes is what `exclude_unmatched=False` will keep (see below). [exclude_unmatched]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether nodes that do not satisfy `conditions=` may end up in the final selection. If `True` (the default), only matching nodes are selected, so a start node whose branches never match contributes nothing. If `False` and `add_to_selection=` is `False`, the deepest unmatched nodes reached (the frontier at `max_steps=`, or the dead-end level where the walk ran out of edges) are selected alongside the matches. If `False` and `add_to_selection=` is `True`, every visited node is added. [add_to_selection]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to select the traversed path or just its endpoints. If `False` (the default), the selection becomes the matching nodes (plus the unmatched frontier when `exclude_unmatched=False`). If `True`, the current selection (the starting nodes) is kept and nodes visited during the walk are added to it; with the default `exclude_unmatched=True` only the visited nodes that match are added, so pair it with `exclude_unmatched=False` to add the whole traversed region. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each node in this small directed graph carries a `value`. Starting at `A` and walking forward until a node has `value >= 5` stops at `E` on one branch and at `D` on the other. `F` also qualifies, but it lies beyond `E`, so it is never reached: ::: {#ed295fc0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) for label, value in [("A", 1), ("B", 2), ("C", 3), ("D", 9), ("E", 7), ("F", 8)]: graph.add_node(label=label, value=value) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "E"), ("C", "D"), ("E", "F")]) def is_big(node_id): return graph.get_node(node_id).attributes["value"] >= 5 start = graph.get_id_from_label("A") graph.select_nodes_by_id([start]).trav_out_until(is_big) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['D', 'E'] ``` ::: ::: Limiting the walk with `max_steps=1` means only `B` is reached, and it does not match. With the default `exclude_unmatched=True` the selection would be empty; setting it to `False` keeps `B` as the frontier where the walk gave up: ::: {#1c05a9da .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.clear_selection() graph.select_nodes_by_id([start]) graph.trav_out_until(is_big, max_steps=1, exclude_unmatched=False) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['B'] ``` ::: ::: Setting `add_to_selection=True` together with `exclude_unmatched=False` keeps every node visited on the way, giving the region between the start and the stopping points (`F` is still excluded because the walk stopped at `E`): ::: {#64d85f01 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.clear_selection() graph.select_nodes_by_id([start]) graph.trav_out_until(is_big, add_to_selection=True, exclude_unmatched=False) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E'] ``` ::: :::
